newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government cracks down on sects among young.
newsitem.headline: French government cracks down on sects among young.

text.p: The French government launched a campaign on Tuesday to crack down on sects which it said had infiltrated children's holiday centres, music classes and choirs in order to recruit young people.
Youth Minister Guy Drut told a news conference that his ministry was reviewing permits granted to some youth associations as part of the prevention campaign.

"Young people, including children, are currently the main target of the sects," Drut said, adding that trained officials would be appointed in each of the ministry's 22 regional branches to keep the public informed.
The ministry will also distribute among sports and young people's associations a report on how sects work and on the threats they pose.
A French parliamentary mission into sects recently listed some 200 organisations and 800 branch offices of suspected sects, adding that sects numbered some 300,000 members.
"An increasing number of associations are set up or infiltrated to serve as recruiting arms. We have to keep that under close control," Drut said.
Several musical groups or choirs had been infiltrated by sects eager to recruit girls from wealthy families, as had some childrens' holiday centres, he said.
France set up a parliamentary mission after 53 people members of the Order of the Solar Temple sect were found dead in a macabre ritual in Switzerland in 1994.
A further 16 charred corpses of members of the doomsday cult were found in the French Alps last December.

On Monday, 23 members of the French Church of Scientology, which says it is a mainstream religion and not a sect, went on trial in the central city of Lyon in a case triggered by the 1988 suicide of a church follower.

Prosecutors accuse the church of "exploiting the good faith and gullibility of its victims for commercial profit, through pseudo-scientific and paramedical means, to their financial detriment and at their medical and psychological risk".
Church of Scientology spokesman Marc Bromberg has denounced the proceeding as "heresy", dubbing the trial "the return of the Inquisition".
